title: I had Claude make my game's trailer by re-rendering real player replays inside the engine, no video editor
author: MightyBig-Dev
selftext:
Play the free demo on Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4923650/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4923650/)

Play in your browser: [https://ninja.mightybig.ca/](https://ninja.mightybig.ca/)

This little trailer for my game Rope Ninja (2D ninja-rope racing) was made with Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code. I never opened a video editor.

Earlier attempts used screen recordings and looked bad. In a raw capture the runner is about 50px tall, so you're mostly watching scenery. So instead of cutting footage, it rendered new footage from inside the game:

• Real runs, re-simulated: it pulled players' recorded runs from my Firebase leaderboard. Runs store their inputs and the sim is deterministic, so it replays them through the actual game. Most finish on the exact same tick as the recorded time.

• A trailer camera in the engine: it added a dev-only capture mode. Playwright drives a headless browser, steps the game one 60fps frame at a time, hides the HUD, and uses a camera that knows the whole path, so it leads the action instead of chasing it. The vertical version is rendered at 1080×1920, not cropped from widescreen.

• Picking the moments: it scored runs for speed, swings and airtime, drew route maps over the level art, and chose shots from those. Characters are cosmetic, so any run can be shown with any of the four runners.

• Cut to the music: it found the beat grid from the kick drum of one of the game's own tracks (\~124 BPM). Cuts land on beats, the frame freezes during the half-second of silence before the drop, and the logo hits on the drop. The rope sounds come from the game's own sound bank, timed to the runner's real fire/hook/release events.

• Graphics and assembly: the titles are an HTML/CSS page rendered frame by frame to a transparent track. Python and ffmpeg do the frame-accurate edit and the loudness pass.

It can't watch video, so it reviewed its own cuts as contact sheets of frames and checked the audio by measurement. My part was feedback: a few rounds of fixes (logo treatment, a runner hidden on the end card, a weak finale shot, a crystal rendering bug in its replay playback), and it re-rendered.

Everything in it is real gameplay rendered by the game. No generated video.

Did I need a trailer for my hobby game... probably not, but I kept seeing neat motion animations done by opus so I figured why not :)

comments.author: Illustrious-Lime-863
comments.body: Cool. Were you into worms? Feels inspired by the rope mechanics in those games (which were a lot of fun)

replies.author: MightyBig-Dev
replies.body: lol to say I was a fan is an understatement!  I played worms 2 ninja rope mode only on Casey’s ladder like 30 years ago. This game is literally a love letter.  So glad you noticed 😇

replies.author: Illustrious-Lime-863
replies.body:
Yeah i remember those tight ninja race modes on the early worms games, one of my earliest online game memories. Turn based is what made it viable to play online basically. Tried to get into it but I gave up, it was so tough. Pure skill issue though because there was some insane talent on there that you were left in awe watching.  

So yeah cool idea to modernize. Give it a lot of love you never know. It could gather an audience and even get popular. Good luck with it

comments.author: phone_radio_tv
comments.body: Looks great, How long did it take & how about cost ?

replies.author: MightyBig-Dev
replies.body: Took about an hour and used very little of my 5h on the 5x plan

comments.author: vincent_sch
comments.body: Re-simulating real runs is smart. You get close shots a screen capture can't give you. Did you pick the runs by hand or by score?

replies.author: MightyBig-Dev
replies.body: I let Claude pick the clips. I need to fix a few toward the end where it chose poorly lol

replies.author: vincent_sch
replies.body: I'd give it a list of shots to keep next time. That should stop it cutting the bits you care about.
